resources.caption: **What orders the elements of a period and of a group within the periodic table.** Along a period, from left to right, the number of electrons in the outer shell rises until an energy level is complete. Down a group, one energy level is added, but every element of a group has the same number of electrons in its outer shell.

resources.caption: **The coordinate (dative) covalent bond that forms the ammonium ion.** The ammonia molecule is neutral, since it has as many electrons as protons. When a dative bond forms with a proton, the ammonium ion results, and its charge is positive.
resources.altText: The coordinate (dative) covalent bond that forms the ammonium ion. The ammonia molecule is neutral, since it has as many electrons as protons. When a dative bond forms with a proton, the ammonium ion results, and its charge is positive.

resources.caption: **How electronegativity sets the polarity of covalent and ionic bonds.** At one end of the scale are the atoms whose similar electronegativities make a non-polar bond; at the other, the ionic bond between very different electronegativities.

resources.caption: **Ionic bonds in water: the salt bridge.** The ionic crystals of sodium chloride dissolve in water thanks to the solvation shell of water molecules around each ion.

resources.caption: **Hydrophobic interactions.** Oil droplets come together through hydrophobic interactions, which keeps their contact surface with water to a minimum.

resources.caption: **Ionisation of a carboxyl group.** At physiological pH the carboxyl behaves as a weak acid and donates a proton to water, which acts as the base. The carboxylate group is the conjugate base, and the water molecule that takes the proton becomes a hydronium ion, an acidic species.

resources.caption: **Nucleophilic and electrophilic centres of the reactive sites.** Nucleophilic groups (electron-rich, such as nitrogen or oxygen) attack electrophilic groups carrying a positive charge or a lower electron density, such as a proton or a carbon.

resources.caption: **Características que determinan el orden de los elementos de un período y de un grupo dentro de la tabla periódica.** A lo largo del período, de izquierda a derecha, aumenta el número de electrones en la última capa hasta completar un nivel de energía. Al descender en un grupo, se aumenta un nivel de energía, pero todos los elementos que pertenecen a un grupo tienen el mismo número de electrones en la última capa.
